tldr: MAgent is a highly scalable many-agent reinforcement learning platform that supports hundreds to millions of agents on a single GPU server, enabling research into artificial collective intelligence and emergent social phenomena such as cooperation, competition, and communication.
contributions: A new research platform, MAgent, dedicated to large-scale many-agent reinforcement learning (hundreds to millions of agents)
High scalability achieving up to one million agents on a single GPU server via network sharing and ID embedding
A reward description language and flexible environment/agent configuration tools for custom environment design
Interactive visual rendering for exploring agent behaviors and emergent collective intelligence
Baseline implementations of parameter-sharing DQN, DRQN, and A2C for benchmarking
Three demo environments (pursuit, gathering, battle) demonstrating emergent cooperation, competition, and hybrid strategies
methods: MAgent uses a C++ engine supporting large-scale gridworld simulation where each agent has a local perspective and optional global information, with actions including moving, turning, or attacking. The platform incorporates a reward description language allowing users to specify rewards via boolean event expressions with logical operations. Parameter-sharing deep RL algorithms (DQN, DRQN, A2C) were implemented, with an embedding added per agent's unique ID to promote diversity. Three environments—pursuit, gathering, and battle—were designed and trained from scratch to observe emergent behaviors.
results: In pursuit, predators learned local cooperation by forming closure patterns to trap prey, earning rewards every step afterward. In gathering, agents learned to compete for limited food resources, rushing to eat and then killing nearby agents to monopolize. In battle, two armies of hundreds of agents each learned both global and local strategies through self-play, including encirclement attacks and guerrilla warfare. MAgent can host up to one million agents on a single GPU server.
limitations: Currently limited to gridworld (discrete) environments; continuous environments are noted as future work
Baseline algorithm implementations are limited to DQN, DRQN, and A2C only
The paper presents demo-level results without comprehensive quantitative benchmarks against other platforms
Only three example environments are demonstrated
